items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0

items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems, jointly interpreting images and natural language queries, hold significant promise across many domains, yet the privacy-sensitive nature of user data creates a fundamental barrier. Centralized training requires access to all data, while federated learning requires each client to host the full model. We propose USPLIT-VQA, a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving VQA in which each client retains the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, keeping raw inputs and labels on the client device. We further introduce Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation (CAWA), a gradientsimilarity-based client scoring mechanism designed to reduce the influence of malicious updates. Experiments on four VQA datasets (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, PathVQA, and VizWiz) with two backbones show accuracy gains over Federated Learning for the Custom model and reduced accuracy for BiomedCLIP under the evaluated fixed split, alongside client memory reductions of up to 5.8X and communication reductions of up to 10.8X. With one malicious client, CAWA reduces the attacker's influence by over 98%, while experiments at higher corruption levels identify its limitations. Reconstruction experiments further show lower inversion quality under the evaluated attacks.
items.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

items.summary: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the second-order total generalized variation functional. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice. Comparisons with related spatial image reconstruction algorithms show comparable reconstruction results. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging, where the proposed functional improves the state of the art.
items.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements

items.summary: This edition presents the current Split-Zero, theta-cohomology and arithmetic-kernel calculations in a research programme on the Riemann zeta function. It publishes the complete 216-page cumulative continuation, the updated 425-page broader research reader, and their proof sources and checks. The purpose is to make the actual calculations readable and reproducible: what was attempted, why that route was chosen, the maps and estimates obtained, and the precise points where the argument remains unfinished. Start with the cumulative calculation reader 14-splitzero-tau-kernel-continuation.pdf is the primary preview. Its 22 proof sections and nine complete source appendices carry the programme from Split-Zero coefficients through theta cohomology, interpolation kernels, chain retractions, homotopy control and the symmetric arithmetic frontier. Earlier source notes retain their own revisions and attribution; the cumulative continuation is not presented as though all its source results originated in one session. Split-Zero coefficients keep the original zero of a ring as a supported element and adjoin a different, external zero, tau. This records the difference between cancelling a coefficient and forgetting the fibre that carried it. Theta cohomology is a specified space of rapidly decreasing functions modulo the image of a specified theta-summation map. Under the stated Mellin transform, that map becomes multiplication by g(s) = 2 xi(s) , where xi is the completed Riemann zeta function. A finite spectral packet records spectral points with their multiplicities, using polynomial quotients and full derivative data rather than discarding repeated-root directions. The calculations construct minimum-norm representatives from the original arithmetic measure, derive full-jet kernel and Gram-inverse formulas, follow nested packets and tensor constructions, and compute the boundary control from the actual theta-derivative sequence. The cumulative reader also develops the relation-layer graph, derivative quotients, norm and Gram-volume identities, and conjugation/reflection-symmetric estimates. Spectral-sum constructions keep the relative variables through matrix weights and complete nilpotent fibres. The quantitative question is how the control form compares with the original arithmetic Gram matrix as the degree and tensor order grow; smallness of one matrix alone is not treated as the required relative estimate. The broader zeta programme 13-main-reader-425p.pdf supplies the surrounding literature reconstruction, CUE random-matrix calculations, arithmetic transforms and source-directed fluid calculations. It includes the all-axis Mellin calculation, complex axial branch points, moving analytic radius and endpoint-residue map for the stated source patch. Those results are described with their source assumptions and maps; they are not recast as a newly constructed zeta-zero witness or an independent proof of the imported fluid existence result. The motivation includes the use of weights in Deligne's Weil II . This programme works out its own analytic spaces, operators, metrics and comparison maps. The complete proofs retain their domains, signs, measures, scalar actions, local units and multiplicities. These are substantive calculations and research attempts, not a claim that an analogy by itself proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. items.summary: Clinical timelines support treatment-window analysis and leakage-free modeling, but discharge summaries often obscure chronology and structured EHR tables describe only part of the patient course. We present a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative event occurrence to its source span and retains that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. We also present GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record, to augment prior matching and temporal assessments. Across six open-weight models and 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, the GLM 5.2 multimodal revision, as compared to its text-only variant, improved temporal agreement without reducing event recovery and performed competitively with clinician annotations, while other model revisions showed smaller gains and lower overall performance. Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement. Blinded human review upheld most GAVEL findings, and controlled adjudication favored multimodal over text-only GLM 5.2 but did not for DeepSeek V3.2. In developing the UID and judge pipeline, we are able to demonstrate 43\% increased event recovery, a framework competitive with clinician annotations, and a system with occurrence-level provenance for both reconstruction and evaluation.
items.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
items.title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content

items.summary: Circular economy is the trend that has emerged as an urgent necessity for manufacturing companies trying to break the linear "take, make, dispose" production cycle. While there is a significant amount of research happening in the circularity domain, the body of knowledge is split and does not necessarily connect with other theories, concepts and with application in different industrial sectors. The aim of this study was to develop an integrated conceptual framework to overcome the existing ambiguities in the field of CE and to facilitate further research while synthesizing the various streams of research on the topic. Methods: The articles were systematically identified from Web of Science and Scopus databases, and then snowballing was performed, in compliance with the PRISMA guidelines, between 2010 and 2025, and resulted in the identification of 100 articles. A tripartite analytical technique based on the use of quantitative bibliometric analysis, qualitative bibliographic content analysis and conceptual mapping was used. Results: The major thematic clusters that emerged were: circular supply chains, design for circularity, industrial symbiosis, Industry 4.0 enablers, policy and governance, performance measurement. The key practices of CE were identified and categorized according to the 4R and 10R frameworks, reverse logistics, industrial symbiosis and digital support for resource recovery at the micro, meso and macro level. The analysis shows that there are organizational, financial, technological and regulatory challenges that remain unaddressed, and that there is a significant lack of empirical evidence on a larger scale. Conclusions: There is a coherent conceptual framework linking CE principles with supply chain operations and Industry 4.0 technologies in this review and it proposes a prioritized future research direction that covers eight critical knowledge gaps. Government, industry and academia receive practical guidance on how to speed circular transitions in manufacturing.

items.title: Circular Economy in Manufacturing Industries: A Literature Review and Future Research Agenda

items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). items.summary: Accurate waveform models are unavailable for many potential sources of gravitational wave transients, motivating searches that do not assume a predefined template family. The Wavelet Detection Filter (WDF) is an unmodeled pipeline that identifies excess energy in the wavelet coefficients of whitened detector data. Here, we develop WDF into a low latency pipeline for both detection and reconstruction and this paper describes and validates that pipeline. We use a zero phase streaming autoregressive whitening filter that preserves transient morphology with a fixed latency and we use the retained wavelet coefficients to provide both a detection statistic and a sparse representation of the signal. By combining coefficients across consecutive analysis windows, the pipeline reconstructs transients longer than a single window. We represent candidate coincidences between detectors with a trigger graph and rank them with supervised and unsupervised graph neural networks (GNNs). We estimate the significance of the ranked coincidences from time shifted data. We validate the pipeline on Gaussian noise colored according to the Advanced LIGO sensitivity curve and on real O4 strain containing compact binary and core collapse supernova injections. Applied to GW250114, WDF identifies the event as the loudest zero lag candidate in the analyzed segment without using waveform templates. We measure the computational cost of the pipeline and the latency it introduces. Both are compatible with a low latency search,so WDF can run on a stream in real time.
items.title: The Wavelet Detection Filter: a real time unmodeled pipeline for gravitational wave transients, ranking coincidences with a graph neural network

items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. L’espressione iniziale U=ΔU=\Delta viene sviluppata attraverso una finestra osservativa finita W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , che determina la risoluzione spaziale e temporale alla quale le differenze possono essere distinte. All’interno di ogni saturazione, le regioni relativamente stabili vengono trattate come convenzioni e non come entità assolute. Ogni convenzione è definita insieme al proprio complemento e acquisisce un bordo operativo. La persistenza viene quindi ricostruita non come immobilità o identità intrinseca, ma come storia di riconferme attraverso letture successive effettuate sotto la stessa finestra. La parte dinamica studia l’evoluzione come processo ricorsivo di riattribuzione locale fra saturazioni successive. Una convenzione risolta può conservare la stessa estensione macroscopica

items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
items.title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

items.summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted mathematical discovery, program search, and formal reasoning motivate a practical design question: how can a long-horizon open problem be reorganized into a broad, falsifiable, and evidence-accountable human–AI search? We present a prospective candidate-engineering framework, grounded in a source-bound retrospective Phase-I design case on arithmetic dynamical structures relevant to the Hilbert–Pólya programme. The paper does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a completed Hilbert–Pólya realization, or a spectral identification of Riemann zeros. The framework has three layers. In Layer 2, mathematician and AI jointly draft and version-freeze an AGENTS.md contract specifying candidate identity, lineage, gates, controls, portfolio policy, and stopping rules. In Layer 3, bounded AI work returns a source-linked evidence handoff for mathematician review. The accompanying roadmap requires a single candidate to establish an endogenous arithmetic source, orbit/repetition ownership, and a same-object zeta or determinant before stronger analytic and operator obligations are considered. The case comprises one early exploration entry and five system-family sessions. Its P1 Wiki retains catalogued provenance records rather than a common score of completed papers, theorems, or Route advances. No source-bound top-level direction documents an integrated same-object A0+A1+A2 chain in one natural candidate. We therefore motivate a broader but lineage-filtered candidate portfolio, screened early for arithmetic, clock, and determinant ownership rather than assembled retrospectively from partial successes. The associated Wiki is a provenance and navigation resource designed to preserve positive local results, controls, scoped failures, and reuse boundaries for subsequent researchers.

items.summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

items.summary: This white paper examines the operational, financial, customer, governance, and leadership consequences arising when customer-facing artificial intelligence makes a commitment the enterprise did not intend to make. The central argument is that a machine-generated promise becomes an enterprise risk when a customer reasonably relies on the output or when organisational systems allow the machine to act on it. The resulting exposure extends beyond hallucination into authority, workflow, customer reliance, execution, redress, and accountability. The paper identifies four escalating customer-AI risk states: Answer, Recommendation, Decision, and Commitment. Exposure increases when generated language moves from information into enterprise obligation. To govern this transition, the paper introduces the Machine Promise Control Architecture, structured around Authoritative Truth, Intent Classification, Authority Envelope, Verification Gate, Escalation and Redress, and Promise Telemetry. Three case studies demonstrate how machine output acquires authority in different operating environments. Cursor shows how generated language became perceived company policy. Rite Aid illustrates machine classification entering customer-facing operational action without adequate safeguards. McDonald’s and IBM demonstrate how conversational interpretation errors propagate into transaction errors, fulfilment problems, rework, and customer impact. Across all three cases, the common failure occurs when machine output acquires credibility, workflow access, decision rights, or customer reliance without corresponding control. The paper further separates AI authority into three distinct permissions: Say, Decide, and Execute. It introduces Promise Surface Area as an executive management model for assessing exposure based on interaction volume, promise-capable intents, authority scope, and consequence. It also applies Six Sigma disciplines through Critical-to-Quality measures, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and the Cost of Poor Promise Quality, linking customer-AI governance directly to operating economics. The central proposition is that customer-facing AI should be governed as a complete decision system rather than as a conversational interface. Enterprises need explicit controls over what AI says, decides, and executes, alongside governed knowledge, deterministic verification, meaningful human escalation, decision lineage, promise-quality measurement, and structured incident recovery. The objective is controlled autonomy, with machine authority expanding only as quickly as the organisation’s ability to govern the resulting commitments.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 18 August 2026.

items.summary: Periodic multilayer mirrors for X-rays require a layer period held to about 0.02 nm, set by deposition rates held in the laboratory's own notebook. A large language model agent was given a target multilayer specification and read access to a laboratory archive. Deposition recipes were authored in the native recipe language of a magnetron sputtering system and submitted through a Model Context Protocol bridge of 17 tools in three tiers, with enforcement held in the control application. The target was a 30-bilayer Ru/C multilayer with a period of 6.85 nm, a pair chosen because each period is fitted as two layers. The agent could write only inside a working project of its own, so it could alter neither the calibration it read nor the measurements that scored it. Mirrors were scored against a human-authored reference by X-ray reflectivity, and the 3% acceptance threshold on relative period difference was fixed before deposition. Across four scored agent-authored depositions the relative period difference fell from 20% on the calibration as given to 2.26% after one measured-feedback iteration and 0.79% after a second. Sixteen failure modes of the agent-facing interface were identified. The result is bounded to the period, pair and chamber observed.
items.title: Agent-authored deposition recipes for X-ray multilayer mirrors: schema-bound LLM control of a magnetron sputtering system with reflectivity-verified outcomes

items.summary: Research artifacts supporting the paper “Cybersecurity Investment Optimization Under Budget Constraints: From QUBO Formulation to Quantum Hardware”. This repository contains the source code, derived experimental instances, raw quantum measurement counts, QUBO/Ising models, QAOA execution outputs, transpiled-circuit metadata, backend information, job identifiers, and processed JSON/CSV results used to reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. The experiments implement an end-to-end cybersecurity investment optimization workflow based on a 0/1 Knapsack formulation transformed into QUBO and Ising representations and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The experimental design includes ideal simulation with Qiskit AerSimulator, architecture-aware noisy emulation using FakeKingston, and execution on the real IBM Quantum ibm_kingston Heron r2 processor. The artifact set covers the 12-qubit reference benchmark, the 20-qubit Safeguard-level stress experiment, and the real-hardware scaling series at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, and 156 logical qubits. For the scaling experiments, the decision variables beyond the original benchmark are explicitly constructed computational replicas used exclusively to evaluate circuit scaling, transpilation overhead, feasibility degradation, and real-QPU behavior; they must not be interpreted as distinct empirical cybersecurity controls. The repository preserves the information necessary to inspect and reproduce the experimental workflow, including optimized and transferred QAOA parameters, shot counts, sampled bitstrings, decoded cybersecurity portfolios, feasibility indicators, QUBO energies, circuit depths, gate counts, two-qubit gate counts, and real-hardware execution metadata. The public-evidence input dataset, CIS_MITRE_QAOA_Public_Evidence, is maintained separately on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/andersonfpdossantos/cis-mitre-qaoa-public-evidence The dataset and these computational artifacts together provide the reproducibility package for the study. No claim of quantum advantage is made; the artifacts are intended to support independent verification, methodological replication, and further investigation of QAOA-based cybersecurity investment optimization.

We present HORIZON, a hierarchical agent that combines symmetry aware spatial perception, dual memory belief tracking, relic centric graph attention, information gain driven exploration, and an opponent conditioned policy mixture. HORIZON separates short horizon control from cross match meta reasoning, while auxiliary belief and world model objectives stabilize learning. Trained with PPO in a large scale JAX simulator, the resulting agent explicitly infers hidden game parameters and opponent style. Experiments show consistent gains in match win rate, episode win rate, adaptation gain, and league rating over strong recurrent and feed forward baselines.
items.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

items.summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.
items.title: Runtime-State Watermarking in Transformers: A Controlled Protocol for Distinguishing Static Self-Simulation from Runtime-State Decodability

items.summary: AI coding assistants are becoming co-authors of production software, yet their evaluation centers on functional correctness, leaving open whether their code differs from human code in the quality dimensions dominating lifecycle cost. We compare human-written and AI-generated code at scale: 787,562 function pairs across Python, Java, and C, each human function mined from open-source repositories paired with implementations generated from its docstring by three AI assistants (OpenAI GPT models, DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen2.5-Coder). We characterize structural complexity and statistical naturalness, and map static-analysis findings onto Orthogonal Defect Classification for defects and the Common Weakness Enumeration for vulnerabilities, making authors and languages directly comparable. AI-generated code is structurally compressed and stylistically templated: roughly half the size and branching of human code, clustering apart at the style level. Defect profiles differ in kind: human code concentrates issues of mature codebases, AI code repetitive boilerplate; security is language-dependent, with LLMs producing more, and more severe, findings in Python and Java but fewer high-severity memory-safety findings than humans in C. Once size is controlled for, complexity metrics carry little signal, while naturalness separates authors. Finally, we release CQBench, a benchmark of 27,346 issue-prone tasks with baselines and an evaluation pipeline for quality assurance and security testing.
items.title: What is the Difference Between Me and You? Benchmarking the Quality Gap Between Human-Written and AI-Generated Code

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: An interface standard is advisory when nothing checks conformance to it, and normative when an external mechanism does. Python's public-interface convention is advisory: PEP 8 recommends that a library declare which symbols are contractual, but nothing enforces it, unlike Java, C++, or Rust. Every library therefore ships two surfaces at once — the declared surface it intends to support and the reachable surface clients can and do import — yet no prior work has measured how much of a library's surface is declared, how much of what clients consume is undeclared, or whether declaration predicts stability. We formalise a five-tier declaration ladder, computable statically from a distribution artifact, and measure it across 163 widely used libraries (81 AI/ML, 82 general-purpose controls) over up to 12 minor releases, together with a uniform sample of 30,000 PyPI projects yielding 14,213 client wheels and 12,704 clients contributing 419,752 import edges. The declared surface is tiny (only 7.4% of reachable symbols); clients over-select it by 5.9×, yet 56.5% (45.3% after a recall correction) of consumed edges remain undeclared, affecting 80.2% of client packages, though clients respect the underscore convention far more than __all__. Declaration status does predict removal — undeclared symbols disappear 1.5–2.5× as often as declared ones — and the AI/ML stack is not worse at signalling than general-purpose Python, only larger and faster-moving. The result is a repeatable, low-cost measurement that a standardisation process could run every release to check whether its own advisory recommendations are being followed.

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.

items.summary: Accurate prediction of equity returns remains a major challenge in computational finance due to the non-stationary, nonlinear, and low signal-to-noise ratio nature of financial time series. This paper proposes a hybrid two-stage architecture that combines a long short-term memory (LSTM) network with an XGBoost gradient-boosted regressor for multi-horizon stock return prediction across a diversified panel of 14 U.S. equities spanning six industry sectors. The LSTM component, comprising two stacked layers with 64 hidden units, processes 60-day sliding windows of five sequential market features to produce 64-dimensional temporal embeddings that encode learned sequential market dynamics. These embeddings are concatenated with 14 hand-crafted technical indicators to form a 78-dimensional hybrid feature vector, which is subsequently passed to an XGBoost regressor tuned via 3-fold cross-validation grid search. The framework is trained on a multi-stock pooled corpus using strict chronological splits and per-stock MinMaxScaling to prevent look-ahead bias, and evaluated across four prediction horizons of 30, 90, 252, and 365 trading days. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid model achieves a test RMSE of 0.0949 on the 30-day horizon, roughly one-third that of the standalone LSTM baseline, while marginally matching or surpassing the XGBoost-Only baseline across the majority of stocks. Directional accuracy rises with horizon length, reaching 97.6% at 365 days; we show, however, that this largely tracks the high base rate of positive long-horizon returns in the sample, and we therefore benchmark directional accuracy against a naive always-positive predictor and treat the above-base-rate gap at short horizons as the more informative signal. A composite investment scoring framework derived from multi-horizon predictions is further proposed to support portfolio ranking and decision support.
items.title: A Hybrid LSTM-XGBoost Framework for Multi-Horizon Stock Return Prediction Across Diversified Equity Portfolios

Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. items.summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. items.summary: This document corresponds to the final release of the CLIM4cities Non-EO Selection and Harmonization Report (NEOR), deliverable D3 of the Work Package (WP)3000, which explains the rationale for choosing the selected non-EO data sources, its harmonisation and processing approach, and its added value for the ML model performance in WP2000. Adding to the provisions made in the original Invitation to Tender (ITT) documentation, CLIM4cities has addressed WP3000 as an overall data collection and pre-processing step of the project, resulting in the final ML model database. Hence, this WP reports all the datasets gathered, their sources and characteristics, along with the full description of the pre-processing sets required for quality control, conversions into derived variables, collocation and harmonisation into the final dataset used for the Machine Learning (ML) training (reported in WP2000, D2 Benchmark Report). The NEOR reports on the following tasks within WP3000 Non-EO and GEO Data Collection, organised into sequential sections of this report: WP3100 - Crowdsourced Data Collection and Quality Assurance, which includes gathering the information from the Citizen Weather Stations (CWS) with available and dense data for the three main cities of study of Denmark - Copenhagen, and at least two out of Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg - with the characterization and application of quality control methodologies. WP3200 - Geospatial Data Collection and Processing, focusing on developing and describing the geospatial data suitable for the development of the CLIM4cities air temperature and land surface temperature (T2m and LST, respectively) models. WP3300 - ML Database Collocation and Harmonization, reporting the final data wrangling steps towards setting up (i) a single collocated regular grid of predictors and (ii) the time series (point-wise, at each CWS station location) to serve as the training input for the CLIM4cities T2m and LST model development.  WP3400 - Data Collection and Exploratory Data Analysis [T2m] in additional FUAs, reports the additional data collection associated with the added functional urban areas, Athens and Seville, as well as the NDVI data used in the updated CERRA based model. Accordingly, the [WP3100]: Crowdsourced Data Collection and Quality Assurance section covers all the acquisition, handling and processing steps of CWS data, including spatial and temporal considerations that determine the evaluation of quality control (QC) of the measurements. In this regard, various statistical methods and novel algorithms for outlier detection were employed, including spatio-temporal relationships between stations, and results compared with the state-of-the-art in-situ observations QC methods. The results show that despite the prevalence of observations that do not meet the QC criteria, the vast volume of CWS available offers a substantial improvement on the observability of the Danish Functional Urban Areas (FUAs - in CLIM4cities, we use this official terminology and the word ‘city interchangeably, as referring to Danish metropolitan areas). Furthermore, in section [WP3200]: Geospatial Data Collection and Processing, the report details all the geospatial data acquisition and wrangling steps of the process. items.summary: Long-running LLM agents require memory mechanisms that maintain coherent internal states across interactions. We study a lifecycle-labeled memory setting in which write episodes provide lifecycle metadata during training, and phase-aware readout is used during evaluation. This setting reflects the need to distinguish information that should remain influential across future interactions from information that should affect only the current context. A mismatch between these lifecycles can cause temporary information to overwrite durable knowledge, leading to behavioral drift in persistent agents. Within this setting, we introduce \textbf{LifeFuse-Mem}, a lifecycle-aware neural memory framework that separates information according to its temporal commitment. LifeFuse-Mem uses dedicated memory components and lifecycle-aware updates to allow stable and transient knowledge to evolve locally without converting temporary context into durable state. On the controlled anti-overwrite benchmark, LifeFuse-Mem improves acquisition-controlled retention and reduces temporary overwrite; on two public long-memory benchmarks, it remains broadly competitive. These results suggest that explicit lifecycle signals can help diagnose and mitigate overwrite in compact online memory.
items.title: LifeFuse-Mem: Lifecycle-Aware State Fusion Against Temporary Overwriting for Long-Term Memory
